name: Harriet Harman
role: Labour MP for Camberwell and Peckham (1982-2024), Deputy Leader (2007-2015), twice acting Leader, Solicitor General, Equality Act 2010 minister; Baroness Harman in the Lords
summary: A Labour feminist and equality campaigner who pushed all-women shortlists, positive action and the Equality Act, and backed the Nordic approach to prostitution. She wants an elected, non-hereditary Lords, supports human rights law and trade unions' rights, and voted to renew Trident.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: As deputy leader she backed a bankers' bonus tax and attacked the cut in the top tax rate, and she voted for a mansion tax (2013) and a higher rate on income over 150,000 pounds (2012).

unions-good.rationale: She pressed for a strong role for trade union equality reps and new rights at work (2010) and voted against tighter regulation of trade union activity.

cut-welfare.rationale: In 23 votes (2010-2024) she voted against reductions in welfare spending and for uprating benefits with prices; as minister she cut lone-parent benefit in 1997, but her later position is against cuts.

surveillance-ok.rationale: She voted for the 2016 Investigatory Powers Bill's bulk communications powers and for Labour's anti-terrorism laws, while pressing for privacy safeguards.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: She said the sex trade exists only because men choose to pay for sex, asked whether to protect women from exploitation or men's right to buy sex ('I certainly know my answer'), and said the Swedish view that prostitution is not a job 'has a point'.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: TheyWorkForYou's summary of her divisions shows she consistently voted for allowing same-sex marriage (five votes for, none against, 2013-2019).

abortion-legal.rationale: She almost always voted for fewer obstacles to abortion access (11 votes for, none against, 2007-2023), including the 2018 decriminalisation motion and the 2021 Northern Ireland regulations.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: She stated support for the full human rights of all people regardless of sexual orientation and built the Equality Act on equal rights across protected groups.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: In 2015 she attacked the government's plan to restrict strikes as an attack on working people's rights, and in 2016 voted against its Trade Union Bill motions.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: She almost always voted for more EU integration (47 for, 8 against, 2007-2020) and in 2015-16 argued for staying in the EU; she never discussed pooled sovereignty in those terms.

death-penalty.rationale: In 2008 she stated total opposition to the death penalty in any country in the world.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: In 2008 she said the most important thing on unwanted pregnancy is good sex education, contraception and responsibility among boys.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: She called the government committed to and proud of its overseas aid record and welcomed the G7's aid commitment, backing the doubled aid budget.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: She voted Aye in July 2016 to renew the UK's Trident nuclear deterrent.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: In her 2022 tribute she praised the Queen for never intervening in politics as 'constitutional alchemy'.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: She extended all-women shortlists to 2030, pressed for positive action to end men-only decision making in business and public bodies, and called 35% women in public appointments 'not good enough'.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: In 2006 she said giving people a legislative role by birth is simply not defensible and that Labour had legislated to end it; in 2025 she moved to end the automatic bishops' seats on the same principle.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Her Equality Act allows tie-break preference for an equally qualified candidate with an under-represented characteristic, and she said it would let employers take positive action for black and Asian employees.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The Equality Act she steered through treats a policy with a disproportionate effect on a protected group as discrimination unless justified, with no need to show intent.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: She voted almost always for equal gay rights (8 for, 1 against, 1998-2019) and in 2009 said there is no place for homophobic prejudice and discrimination, so she opposes criminalising same-sex relations.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: In 2022 she said the fundamentals of the Gender Recognition Act and the Equality Act remain sound, while favouring narrow single-sex exceptions.

assisted-dying.rationale: The recorded votes show her voting for allowing terminally ill people to be given assistance to end their life.

second-chamber.rationale: She voted for a wholly elected House of Lords (2007-2012) and in 2025 described the Lords as a revising chamber whose legitimacy matters, so she favours reforming a second chamber rather than abolishing it.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: In 2015 she opposed cutting tax credits, saying a higher minimum wage would not make up for the loss to working families.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: She voted Aye in July 2016 to renew Trident rather than disarm.

women-suffrage.rationale: She spoke of women's right to vote and to vote for women and men as basic, and campaigned for their equal presence in the Commons.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: As Minister for Women and Equalities she defended the Equality and Human Rights Commission as an important body and later backed a permanent Women and Equalities Committee.

national-church-status.rationale: In January 2025 she moved an amendment to end the 26 Church of England bishops' automatic seats in the Lords, opposing that special legal status in the legislature.

notes: Hansard speeches were searched through the Parliament Hansard API (Commons only; her Lords contributions are not indexed there, so 2025 Lords remarks rest on a Humanists UK report) and Commons divisions from 2010. Searched themes: economy, liberty, society, world, government, ecology, technology, means. Gap-fill pass added TheyWorkForYou vote summaries (via the Wayback Machine) and more Hansard searches (marriage, EU, minimum wage, NHS, immigration, climate, tuition fees, inheritance tax, childcare, divorce, Iraq, aid). Iraq 2003: she voted for the war, but no statement matches that vote or the 2015 Syria refugee debate. No match found for the 2015 welfare bill abstention beyond her stated support for a household benefit cap. Left null: NHS, immigration levels, language, minimum wage rise, climate, free college, inheritance tax, care, marriage law, monarchy, wealth and liberty. Thin themes: ecology, technology, means.
